    36	JERICHO_PATH = importlib.resources.files("jericho")
    37	FROTZ_LIB_PATH = os.path.join(JERICHO_PATH, 'libfrotz.so')

    39	# The buffer size for actions in frotz. -2 to allow for newline and null terminator.
    40	INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE = 200 - 2
    41	
    42	# Function to unload a shared library.
    43	dlclose_func = CDLL(None).dlclose  # This WON'T work on Win
    44	dlclose_func.argtypes = [c_void_p]

    46	
    47	def init_worker(story, seed):
    48	    """ Worker that will be used to test candidate actions. """
    49	    worker.env = FrotzEnv(story, seed)
    50	
    51	
    52	def worker(data):
    53	    """ Worker that will be used to test candidate actions. """
    54	    state, candidate_actions, use_ctypes = data
    55	    worker.env.set_state(state)
    56	    return worker.env._filter_candidate_actions(candidate_actions, use_ctypes=use_ctypes, use_parallel=False)
    57	
    58	
    59	class ZObject(Structure):
    60	    """
    61	    A Z-Machine Object contains the following fields:
    62	
    63	    :param num: Object number
    64	    :type num: int
    65	    :param name: Short object name
    66	    :type name: string
    67	    :param parent: Object number of parent
    68	    :type parent: int
    69	    :param sibling: Object number of sibling
    70	    :type sibling: int
    71	    :param child: Object number of child
    72	    :type child: int
    73	    :param attr: 32-bit array of object attributes
    74	    :type attr: array
    75	    :param properties: object properties
    76	    :type properties: list
    77	
    78	    :Example:
    79	
    80	    >>> from jericho import *
    81	    >>> env = FrotzEnv('zork1.z5')
    82	    >>> env.get_player_object()
    83	    Obj4: cretin Parent180 Sibling181 Child0 Attributes [7, 9, 14, 30] Properties [18, 17, 7]
    84	
    85	    """
    86	    _fields_ = [("num",        c_int),
    87	                ("_name",      c_char*64),
    88	                ("parent",     c_int),
    89	                ("sibling",    c_int),
    90	                ("child",      c_int),
    91	                ("_attr",      c_byte*4),
    92	                ("properties", c_ubyte*16)]
    93	
    94	    def __init__(self):
    95	        self.num = -1
    96	
    97	    def __str__(self):
    98	        return "Obj{}: {} Parent{} Sibling{} Child{} Attributes {} Properties {}"\
    99	            .format(self.num, self.name, self.parent, self.sibling, self.child,
   100	                    np.nonzero(self.attr)[0].tolist(), [p for p in self.properties if p != 0])
   101	
   102	    def __repr__(self):
   103	        return str(self)
   104	
   105	    def __eq__(self, other):
   106	        # Equality check doesn't compare siblings and children. This
   107	        # makes comparison among object trees more flexible.
   108	        if isinstance(self, other.__class__):
   109	            return self.num   == other.num      and \
   110	                self.name     == other.name     and \
   111	                self.parent   == other.parent   and \
   112	                self._attr[0] == other._attr[0] and \
   113	                self._attr[1] == other._attr[1] and \
   114	                self._attr[2] == other._attr[2] and \
   115	                self._attr[3] == other._attr[3] and \
   116	                self.properties[:] == other.properties[:]
   117	        return False
   118	
   119	    def __hash__(self):
   120	        return hash(str(self))
   121	
   122	    @property
   123	    def name(self):
   124	        return self._name.decode('cp1252')
   125	
   126	    @property
   127	    def attr(self):
   128	        return np.unpackbits(np.array(self._attr, dtype=np.uint8))
   129	
   130	
   131	class DictionaryWord(Structure):
   132	    """
   133	    A word recognized by a game's parser.
   134	
   135	    :param word: The dictionary word itself.
   136	    :type word: string
   137	    :param is_noun: Is the word a noun.
   138	    :type is_noun: boolean
   139	    :param is_verb: Is the word a verb.
   140	    :type is_verb: boolean
   141	    :param is_prep: Is the word a preposition.
   142	    :type is_prep: boolean
   143	    :param is_meta: Used for meta commands like 'verbose' and 'script'
   144	    :type is_meta: boolean
   145	    :param is_plural: Used for pluralized nouns (e.g. bookcases, rooms)
   146	    :type is_plural: boolean
   147	    :param is_dir: Used for direction words (e.g. north, aft)
   148	    :type is_dir: boolean
   149	    :param is_special: Used for special commands like 'again' which repeats last action.
   150	    :type is_special: boolean
   151	
   152	    :Example:
   153	
   154	    >>> from jericho import *
   155	    >>> env = FrotzEnv('zork1.z5')
   156	    >>> vocab = env.get_dictionary()
   157	    [$ve, ., ,, ", a, across, activa, advent, ... zork, zorkmi, zzmgck]
   158	    >>> [w for w in vocab if w.is_noun]
   159	    [advent, advert, air, air-p, altar, art, aviato, ax, axe, bag, ... ]
   160	    >>> [w for w in vocab if w.is_adj]
   161	    [ancien, antiqu, bare, beauti, birds, black, bloody, blue, ... ]
   162	
   163	    .. note:: Many parsers will recognize only the first six or nine characters of\
   164	    each word. For example `northwest` is functionally equivalent to `northw`.
   165	
   166	    .. warning:: Not all games specify the parts of speech for dictionary words.
   167	
   168	    """
   169	    _fields_ = [("_word",      c_char*10),
   170	                ("is_noun",    c_bool),
   171	                ("is_verb",    c_bool),
   172	                ("is_prep",    c_bool),
   173	                ("is_meta",    c_bool),
   174	                ("is_plural",  c_bool),
   175	                ("is_dir",     c_bool),
   176	                ("is_adj",     c_bool),
   177	                ("is_special", c_bool)]
   178	
   179	    def __init__(self, word, is_noun=False, is_verb=False,
   180	                 is_prep=False, is_meta=False, is_plural=False,
   181	                 is_dir=False, is_adj=False, is_special=False):
   182	        super(DictionaryWord, self).__init__(word.encode('utf-8'),
   183	                                             is_noun, is_verb,
   184	                                             is_prep, is_meta,
   185	                                             is_plural, is_dir,
   186	                                             is_adj, is_special)
   187	
   188	    def __repr__(self):
   189	        return self.word
   190	
   191	    @property
   192	    def word(self):
   193	        return self._word.decode('cp1252')
   194	
   195	    def pos(self):
   196	        pos = []
   197	        if self.is_noun:
   198	            pos.append('noun')
   199	        if self.is_verb:
   200	            pos.append('verb')
   201	        if self.is_prep:
   202	            pos.append('prep')
   203	        if self.is_meta:
   204	            pos.append('meta')
   205	        if self.is_plural:
   206	            pos.append('plural')
   207	        if self.is_dir:
   208	            pos.append('dir')
   209	        if self.is_adj:
   210	            pos.append('adj')
   211	        if self.is_special:
   212	            pos.append('special')
   213	        return pos
   214	
   215	
   216	def _load_frotz_lib():
   217	    """ Loads a copy of frotz's shared library. """
   218	
   219	    # Make a copy of libfrotz.so before loading it to avoid concurrency issues.
   220	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
   221	        frotz_lib_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, 'libfrotz.so')
   222	        shutil.copyfile(FROTZ_LIB_PATH, frotz_lib_path)
   223	        frotz_lib = cdll.LoadLibrary(frotz_lib_path)
   224	
   225	    frotz_lib.setup.argtypes = [c_char_p, c_int, c_char_p, c_int]
   226	    frotz_lib.setup.restype = c_char_p
   227	    frotz_lib.shutdown.argtypes = []
   228	    frotz_lib.shutdown.restype = None
   229	    frotz_lib.step.argtypes = [c_char_p]
   230	    frotz_lib.step.restype = c_char_p
   231	    frotz_lib.save.argtypes = [c_char_p]
   232	    frotz_lib.save.restype = int
   233	    frotz_lib.restore.argtypes = [c_char_p]
   234	    frotz_lib.restore.restype = int
   235	    frotz_lib.get_object.argtypes = [c_void_p, c_int]
   236	    frotz_lib.get_object.restype = None
   237	    frotz_lib.get_num_world_objs.argtypes = []
   238	    frotz_lib.get_num_world_objs.restype = int
   239	    frotz_lib.get_world_objects.argtypes = [POINTER(ZObject), c_int]
   240	    frotz_lib.get_world_objects.restype = None
   241	    frotz_lib.get_self_object_num.argtypes = []
   242	    frotz_lib.get_self_object_num.restype = int
   243	    frotz_lib.get_moves.argtypes = []
   244	    frotz_lib.get_moves.restype = int
   245	    frotz_lib.get_score.argtypes = []
   246	    frotz_lib.get_score.restype = c_short
   247	    frotz_lib.get_max_score.argtypes = []
   248	    frotz_lib.get_max_score.restype = int
   249	    frotz_lib.save_str.argtypes = [c_void_p]
   250	    frotz_lib.save_str.restype = int
   251	    frotz_lib.restore_str.argtypes = [c_void_p]
   252	    frotz_lib.restore_str.restype = int
   253	    frotz_lib.world_changed.argtypes = []
   254	    frotz_lib.world_changed.restype = int
   255	    frotz_lib.get_cleaned_world_diff.argtypes = [c_void_p, c_void_p]
   256	    frotz_lib.get_cleaned_world_diff.restype = None
   257	    frotz_lib.game_over.argtypes = []
   258	    frotz_lib.game_over.restype = int
   259	    frotz_lib.victory.argtypes = []
   260	    frotz_lib.victory.restype = int
   261	    frotz_lib.halted.argtypes = []
   262	    frotz_lib.halted.restype = int
   263	
   264	    frotz_lib.filter_candidate_actions.argtypes = [c_char_p, c_char_p, c_void_p]
   265	    frotz_lib.filter_candidate_actions.restype = int
   266	
   267	    frotz_lib.getRAMSize.argtypes = []
   268	    frotz_lib.getRAMSize.restype = int
   269	    frotz_lib.getRAM.argtypes = [c_void_p]
   270	    frotz_lib.getRAM.restype = None
   271	
   272	    frotz_lib.get_special_ram_size.argtypes = []
   273	    frotz_lib.get_special_ram_size.restype = int
   274	    frotz_lib.get_special_ram.argtypes = [c_void_p]
   275	    frotz_lib.get_special_ram.restype = None
   276	
   277	    frotz_lib.get_narrative_text.argtypes = []
   278	    frotz_lib.get_narrative_text.restype = c_char_p
   279	    frotz_lib.set_narrative_text.argtypes = [c_char_p]
   280	    frotz_lib.set_narrative_text.restype = None
   281	
   282	    frotz_lib.getPC.argtypes = []
   283	    frotz_lib.getPC.restype = int
   284	    frotz_lib.setPC.argtypes = [c_int]
   285	    frotz_lib.setPC.restype = None
   286	
   287	    frotz_lib.getSP.argtypes = []
   288	    frotz_lib.getSP.restype = int
   289	    frotz_lib.setSP.argtypes = [c_int]
   290	    frotz_lib.setSP.restype = None
   291	
   292	    frotz_lib.getFP.argtypes = []
   293	    frotz_lib.getFP.restype = int
   294	    frotz_lib.setFP.argtypes = [c_int]
   295	    frotz_lib.setFP.restype = None
   296	
   297	    frotz_lib.getFrameCount.argtypes = []
   298	    frotz_lib.getFrameCount.restype = int
   299	    frotz_lib.setFrameCount.argtypes = [c_int]
   300	    frotz_lib.setFrameCount.restype = None
   301	
   302	    frotz_lib.getRngA.argtypes = []
   303	    frotz_lib.getRngA.restype = np.int64
   304	    frotz_lib.getRngInterval.argtypes = []
   305	    frotz_lib.getRngInterval.restype = int
   306	    frotz_lib.getRngCounter.argtypes = []
   307	    frotz_lib.getRngCounter.restype = int
   308	    frotz_lib.setRng.argtypes = [c_long, c_int, c_int]
   309	    frotz_lib.setRng.restype = None
   310	
   311	    frotz_lib.getRAMSize.argtypes = []
   312	    frotz_lib.getRAMSize.restype = int
   313	    frotz_lib.getRAM.argtypes = [c_void_p]
   314	    frotz_lib.getRAM.restype = None
   315	    frotz_lib.setRAM.argtypes = [c_void_p]
   316	    frotz_lib.setRAM.restype = None
   317	    frotz_lib.getStack.argtypes = [c_void_p]
   318	    frotz_lib.getStack.restype = None
   319	    frotz_lib.setStack.argtypes = [c_void_p]
   320	    frotz_lib.setStack.restype = None
   321	    frotz_lib.getStackSize.argtypes = []
   322	    frotz_lib.getStackSize.restype = int
   323	
   324	    frotz_lib.get_opcode.argtypes = []
   325	    frotz_lib.get_opcode.restype = int
   326	    frotz_lib.set_opcode.argtypes = [c_int]
   327	    frotz_lib.set_opcode.restype = None
   328	
   329	    frotz_lib.disassemble.argtypes = [c_char_p]
   330	    frotz_lib.disassemble.restype = None
   331	    frotz_lib.is_supported.argtypes = [c_char_p]
   332	    frotz_lib.is_supported.restype = int
   333	    frotz_lib.get_dictionary_word_count.argtypes = [c_char_p]
   334	    frotz_lib.get_dictionary_word_count.restype = int
   335	    frotz_lib.get_dictionary.argtypes = [POINTER(DictionaryWord), c_int]
   336	    frotz_lib.get_dictionary.restype = None
   337	    frotz_lib.ztools_cleanup.argtypes = []
   338	    frotz_lib.ztools_cleanup.restype = None
   339	    return frotz_lib

   341	
   342	def _load_bindings(md5hash):
   343	    """
   344	    Loads information pertaining to the game corresponding to the provided md5 hash.
   345	    Returns a dictionary with the following keys:
   346	
   347	    - `name`: Name of the game. E.g. `zork1`
   348	    - `rom`: Name of the file used to load the game. E.g. `zork1.z5`
   349	    - `walkthrough`: A walkthrough for the game.
   350	    - `seed`: Seed necessary to replicate the walkthrough.
   351	    - `grammar`: List of action templates for the game.
   352	    - `max_word_length`: Maximum number of characters per word recognized by the parser.
   353	
   354	    :param md5hash: A game's md5 hash.
   355	    :type md5hash: string
   356	
   357	    :returns: Dictionary containing game-specific bindings if it exists.
   358	              Otherwise, an empty dictionary.
   359	    """
   360	    return defines.BINDINGS_DICT.get(md5hash, {})
   361	
   362	
   363	class UnsupportedGameWarning(UserWarning):
   364	    pass
   365	
   366	
   367	class TruncatedInputActionWarning(UserWarning):
   368	    pass
   369	
   370	
   371	class FrotzEnv():
   372	    """
   373	    The Frotz Environment is a fast interface to Z-Machine games.
   374	
   375	    :param story_file: Path to a Z-machine rom file (.z3/.z5/.z6/.z8).
   376	    :param seed: Seed the random number generator used by the emulator.
   377	                 Default: use walkthrough's seed if it exists,
   378	                          otherwise use value of -1 which changes with time.
   379	    :type story_file: path
   380	    :type seed: int
   381	
   382	    """
   383	    def __init__(self, story_file, seed=None):
   384	        self._cache = {}
   385	        self.frotz_lib = _load_frotz_lib()
   386	        self._bindings = None
   387	        self.load(story_file, seed)
   388	
   389	    def __del__(self):
   390	        if hasattr(self, 'frotz_lib'):
   391	            self.frotz_lib.shutdown()
   392	            dlclose_func(self.frotz_lib._handle)
   393	
   394	    def load(self, story_file, seed=None):
   395	        '''
   396	        Loads a Z-Machine game.
   397	
   398	        :param story_file: Path to a Z-machine rom file (.z3/.z5/.z6/.z8).
   399	        :param seed: Seed the random number generator used by the emulator.
   400	                    Default: use walkthrough's seed if it exists,
   401	                            otherwise use value of -1 which changes with time.
   402	        :type story_file: path
   403	        :type seed: int
   404	        '''
   405	        self.story_file = story_file.encode('utf-8')
   406	
   407	        if story_file not in self._cache:
   408	            if not os.path.isfile(story_file):
   409	                raise FileNotFoundError(story_file)
   410	
   411	            with open(story_file, "rb") as f:
   412	                rom = f.read()
   413	
   414	            self.is_fully_supported = bool(self.frotz_lib.is_supported(self.story_file))
   415	            if not self.is_fully_supported:
   416	                msg = ("Game '{}' is not fully supported. Score, move, change"
   417	                    " detection will be disabled.").format(story_file)
   418	                warnings.warn(msg, UnsupportedGameWarning)
   419	
   420	            md5hash = hashlib.md5(rom).hexdigest()
   421	            self._bindings = _load_bindings(md5hash)
   422	            self.act_gen = TemplateActionGenerator(self.bindings) if self.bindings else None
   423	
   424	            self._cache[story_file] = (rom, self.bindings, self.act_gen)
   425	
   426	        rom, self._bindings, self.act_gen = self._cache[story_file]
   427	
   428	        self.seed(seed)
   429	        self.frotz_lib.setup(self.story_file, self._seed, rom, len(rom))
   430	        self.player_obj_num = self.frotz_lib.get_self_object_num()
   431	
   432	    def seed(self, seed=None):
   433	        '''
   434	        Changes seed used for the emulator's random number generator.
   435	
   436	        :param seed: Seed the random number generator used by the emulator.
   437	                     Default: use walkthrough's seed if it exists,
   438	                              otherwise use value of -1 which changes with time.
   439	        :returns: The value of the seed.
   440	
   441	        .. note:: :meth:`jericho.FrotzEnv.reset()` must be called before the seed takes effect.
   442	
   443	        '''
   444	        seed = seed or self.bindings.get('seed', -1)
   445	        self._seed = seed
   446	        return seed
   447	
   448	    def reset(self):
   449	        '''
   450	        Resets the game.
   451	
   452	        :param use_walkthrough_seed: Seed the emulator to reproduce the walkthrough.
   453	        :returns: A tuple containing the initial observation,\
   454	        and a dictionary of info.
   455	        :rtype: string, dictionary
   456	
   457	        '''
   458	        self.close()
   459	        rom, _, _ = self._cache[self.story_file.decode()]
   460	        obs_ini = self.frotz_lib.setup(self.story_file, self._seed, rom, len(rom)).decode('cp1252')
   461	        score = self.frotz_lib.get_score()
   462	        return obs_ini, {'moves':self.get_moves(), 'score':score}
   463	
   464	    def step(self, action):
   465	        '''
   466	        Takes an action and returns the next state, reward, termination
   467	
   468	        :param action: Text command to send to the interpreter.
   469	        :type action: string
   470	
   471	        :returns: A tuple containing the game's textual response to the action,\
   472	        the immediate reward, a boolean indicating whether the game is over,\
   473	        and a dictionary of info.
   474	        :rtype: string, float, boolean, dictionary
   475	
   476	        Note:
   477	        - The action is converted to bytes and truncated to 198 characters.
   478	        '''
   479	        action_bytes = action.encode('utf-8')
   480	        if len(action_bytes) > INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE:
   481	            action_bytes = action_bytes[:INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE]
   482	            msg = ("Once converted to bytes, actions should have less than 198 characters."
   483	                   " Action '{}' was truncated to '{}'.".format(action, action_bytes.decode()))
   484	            warnings.warn(msg, TruncatedInputActionWarning)
   485	
   486	        old_score = self.frotz_lib.get_score()
   487	        next_state = self.frotz_lib.step(action_bytes + b'\n').decode('cp1252')
   488	        score = self.frotz_lib.get_score()
   489	        reward = score - old_score
   490	        return next_state, reward, (self.game_over() or self.victory()),\
   491	            {'moves':self.get_moves(), 'score':score}
   492	
   493	    def close(self):
   494	        ''' Cleans up the FrotzEnv, freeing any allocated memory. '''
   495	        self.frotz_lib.shutdown()
   496	
   497	    @property
   498	    def bindings(self):
   499	        """
   500	        Gets information pertaining to the currently loaded game.
   501	        Returns a dictionary with the following keys:
   502	
   503	        - `name`: Name of the game. E.g. `zork1`
   504	        - `rom`: Name of the file used to load the game. E.g. `zork1.z5`
   505	        - `walkthrough`: A walkthrough for the game.
   506	        - `seed`: Seed necessary to replicate the walkthrough.
   507	        - `grammar`: List of action templates for the game.
   508	        - `max_word_length`: Maximum number of characters per word recognized by the parser.
   509	
   510	        :returns: Dictionary containing game-specific bindings if it exists.
   511	                  Otherwise, an empty dictionary.
   512	
   513	        :Example:
   514	
   515	        >>> import jericho
   516	        >>> env = jericho.FrotzEnv('zork1')
   517	        >>> env.bindings
   518	        {
   519	        'name': 'zork1',
   520	        'rom': 'zork1.z5',
   521	        'seed': 12,
   522	        'max_word_length': 6,
   523	        'minimal_actions': 'Ulysses/wait/pray/inventory/go down/...',
   524	        'grammar': 'again/g;answer/reply;back;barf/chomp/...',
   525	        'walkthrough': 'N/N/U/Get egg/D/S/E/Open window/...'
   526	        }
   527	
   528	        .. note:: Walkthroughs are defined for only a few games.
   529	        """
   530	        return self._bindings
   531	
   532	    def get_dictionary(self):
   533	        ''' Returns a list of :class:`jericho.DictionaryWord` words recognized\
   534	        by the game's parser. See :doc:`dictionary`. '''
   535	        word_count = self.frotz_lib.get_dictionary_word_count(self.story_file)
   536	        words = (DictionaryWord * word_count)()
   537	        self.frotz_lib.get_dictionary(words, word_count)
   538	        self.frotz_lib.ztools_cleanup()
   539	        return list(words)
   540	
   541	    def get_walkthrough(self):
   542	        ''' Returns the walkthrough for the game.
   543	
   544	        :returns: A list containing walkthrough action strings needed to complete the game.
   545	
   546	        .. note:: To reproduce the walkthrough it's also necessary to reset the environment\
   547	        with use_walkthrough_seed=True.
   548	        '''
   549	        if not self.is_fully_supported or not self.bindings:
   550	            warnings.warn('Unable to retrieve walkthrough for this game.', UnsupportedGameWarning)
   551	            return []
   552	        return self.bindings['walkthrough'].split('/')
   553	
   554	    def get_valid_actions(self, use_object_tree=True, use_ctypes=True, use_parallel=True):
   555	        """
   556	        Attempts to generate a set of unique valid actions from the current game state.
   557	
   558	        :param use_object_tree: Query the :doc:`object_tree` for names of surrounding objects.
   559	        :type use_object_tree: boolean
   560	        :param use_ctypes: Uses the optimized ctypes implementation of valid action filtering.
   561	        :type use_ctypes: boolean
   562	        :param use_parallel: Uses the parallized implementation of valid action filtering.
   563	        :type use_parallel: boolean
   564	        :returns: A list of valid actions.
   565	
   566	        """
   567	        if not self.is_fully_supported or not self.act_gen:
   568	            warnings.warn('Unable to find valid actions in an unsupported game.', UnsupportedGameWarning)
   569	            return []
   570	
   571	        interactive_objs  = self._identify_interactive_objects(use_object_tree=use_object_tree)
   572	        best_obj_names    = self._score_object_names(interactive_objs)
   573	        candidate_actions = self.act_gen.generate_actions(best_obj_names)
   574	        diff2acts         = self._filter_candidate_actions(candidate_actions, use_ctypes, use_parallel)
   575	        valid_actions = [max(v, key=utl.verb_usage_count) for v in diff2acts.values()]
   576	        return valid_actions
   577	
   578	    def set_state(self, state):
   579	        '''
   580	        Sets the game's internal state.
   581	
   582	        :param state: Tuple of (ram, stack, pc, sp, fp, frame_count, rng) as\
   583	        obtained by :meth:`jericho.FrotzEnv.get_state`.
   584	        :type state: tuple
   585	
   586	        >>> from jericho import *
   587	        >>> env = FrotzEnv(rom_path)
   588	        >>> state = env.get_state()
   589	        >>> env.step('attack troll') # Oops!
   590	        'You swing and miss. The troll neatly removes your head.'
   591	        >>> env.set_state(state) # Whew, let's try something else
   592	
   593	        '''
   594	        ram, stack, pc, sp, fp, frame_count, opcode, rng, narrative = state
   595	        self.frotz_lib.setRng(*rng)
   596	        self.frotz_lib.setRAM(as_ctypes(ram))
   597	        self.frotz_lib.setStack(as_ctypes(stack))
   598	        self.frotz_lib.setPC(pc)
   599	        self.frotz_lib.setSP(sp)
   600	        self.frotz_lib.setFP(fp)
   601	        self.frotz_lib.set_opcode(opcode)
   602	        self.frotz_lib.setFrameCount(frame_count)
   603	        self.frotz_lib.set_narrative_text(narrative)
   604	
   605	    def get_state(self):
   606	        '''
   607	        Returns the internal game state. This state can be subsequently restored
   608	        using :meth:`jericho.FrotzEnv.set_state`.
   609	
   610	        :returns: Tuple of (ram, stack, pc, sp, fp, frame_count, rng).
   611	
   612	        >>> from jericho import *
   613	        >>> env = FrotzEnv(rom_path)
   614	        >>> state = env.get_state()
   615	        >>> env.step('attack troll') # Oops!
   616	        'You swing and miss. The troll neatly removes your head.'
   617	        >>> env.set_state(state) # Whew, let's try something else
   618	
   619	        '''
   620	        ram = np.zeros(self.frotz_lib.getRAMSize(), dtype=np.uint8)
   621	        stack = np.zeros(self.frotz_lib.getStackSize(), dtype=np.uint8)
   622	        self.frotz_lib.getRAM(as_ctypes(ram))
   623	        self.frotz_lib.getStack(as_ctypes(stack))
   624	        pc = self.frotz_lib.getPC()
   625	        sp = self.frotz_lib.getSP()
   626	        fp = self.frotz_lib.getFP()
   627	        opcode = self.frotz_lib.get_opcode()
   628	        frame_count = self.frotz_lib.getFrameCount()
   629	        rng = self.frotz_lib.getRngA(), self.frotz_lib.getRngInterval(), self.frotz_lib.getRngCounter()
   630	        narrative = self.frotz_lib.get_narrative_text()
   631	        state = ram, stack, pc, sp, fp, frame_count, opcode, rng, narrative
   632	        return state
   633	
   634	    def get_max_score(self):
   635	        ''' Returns the integer maximum possible score for the game. '''
   636	        return self.frotz_lib.get_max_score()
   637	
   638	    def copy(self):
   639	        ''' Forks this FrotzEnv instance. '''
   640	        state = self.get_state()
   641	        env = FrotzEnv(self.story_file.decode(), seed=self._seed)
   642	        env.set_state(state)
   643	        return env
   644	
   645	    def get_player_location(self):
   646	        ''' Returns the :class:`jericho.ZObject` corresponding to the location of the player in the world. '''
   647	        parent = self.get_player_object().parent
   648	        return self.get_object(parent)
   649	
   650	    def get_object(self, obj_num):
   651	        '''
   652	        Returns a :class:`jericho.ZObject` with the corresponding number or `None` if the object\
   653	        doesn't exist in the :doc:`object_tree`.
   654	
   655	        :param obj_num: Object number between 0 and len(get_world_objects()).
   656	        :type obj_num: int
   657	        '''
   658	        obj = ZObject()
   659	        self.frotz_lib.get_object(byref(obj), obj_num)
   660	        if obj.num < 0:
   661	            return None
   662	        return obj
   663	
   664	    def get_world_objects(self, clean=False):
   665	        ''' Returns an array containing all the :class:`jericho.ZObject` in the game.
   666	
   667	        :param clean: If True, disconnects noisy objects like Zork1's thief from\
   668	        the Object Tree. This is mainly useful if using world objects as an\
   669	        indication of unique game state.
   670	        :type clean: Boolean
   671	
   672	        :returns: Array of :class:`jericho.ZObject`.
   673	
   674	        :Example:
   675	
   676	        >>> from jericho import *
   677	        >>> env = FrotzEnv('zork1.z5')
   678	        >>> env.get_world_objects()
   679	         Obj0:  Parent0 Sibling0 Child0 Attributes [] Properties [],
   680	         Obj1: pair hands Parent247 Sibling2 Child0 Attributes [14, 28] Properties [18, 16],
   681	         Obj2: zorkmid Parent247 Sibling3 Child0 Attributes [] Properties [18, 17],
   682	         Obj3: way Parent247 Sibling5 Child0 Attributes [14] Properties [18, 17, 16],
   683	         Obj4: cretin Parent180 Sibling181 Child0 Attributes [7, 9, 14, 30] Properties [18, 17, 7],
   684	         Obj5: you Parent247 Sibling6 Child0 Attributes [30] Properties [18, 17],
   685	         ...
   686	         Obj250: board Parent249 Sibling73 Child0 Attributes [14] Properties [18, 17]
   687	
   688	        '''
   689	        n_objs = self.frotz_lib.get_num_world_objs()
   690	        objs = (ZObject * (n_objs+1))() # Add extra spot for zero'th object
   691	        self.frotz_lib.get_world_objects(objs, clean)
   692	        return objs
   693	
   694	    def get_player_object(self):
   695	        ''' Returns the :class:`jericho.ZObject` corresponding to the player. '''
   696	        return self.get_object(self.player_obj_num)
   697	
   698	    def get_inventory(self):
   699	        ''' Returns a list of :class:`jericho.ZObject` in the player's posession. '''
   700	        inventory = []
   701	        item_nb = self.get_player_object().child
   702	        while item_nb > 0:
   703	            item = self.get_object(item_nb)
   704	            if not item:
   705	                break
   706	            inventory.append(item)
   707	            item_nb = item.sibling
   708	        return inventory
   709	
   710	    def get_world_state_hash(self):
   711	        """ Returns a MD5 hash of the clean world-object-tree. Such a hash may be
   712	        useful for identifying when the agent has reached new states or returned
   713	        to existing ones.
   714	
   715	        :Example:
   716	
   717	        >>> env = FrotzEnv('zork1.z5')
   718	        >>> env.reset()
   719	        # Start at West of the House with the following hash
   720	        >>> env.get_world_state_hash()
   721	        '79c750fff4368efef349b02ff50ffc23'
   722	        >>> env.step('n')
   723	        # Moving to North of House changes the hash
   724	        >>> get_world_state_hash(env)
   725	        '8a3a8538c0019a69128f755e4b719fbd'
   726	        >>> env.step('w')
   727	        # Moving back to West of House we recover the original hash
   728	        >>> env.get_world_state_hash()
   729	        '79c750fff4368efef349b02ff50ffc23'
   730	
   731	        """
   732	        import hashlib
   733	        world_objs_str = ', '.join([str(o) for o in self.get_world_objects(clean=True)])
   734	        special_ram_addrs = self._get_special_ram()
   735	        world_state_str = world_objs_str + str(special_ram_addrs)
   736	        m = hashlib.md5()
   737	        m.update(world_state_str.encode('utf-8'))
   738	        return m.hexdigest()
   739	
   740	    def get_moves(self):
   741	        ''' Returns the integer number of moves taken by the player in the current episode. '''
   742	        return self.frotz_lib.get_moves()
   743	
   744	    def get_score(self):
   745	        ''' Returns the integer current game score. '''
   746	        return self.frotz_lib.get_score()
   747	
   748	    def victory(self):
   749	        ''' Returns `True` if the game is over and the player has won. '''
   750	        return self.frotz_lib.victory() > 0
   751	
   752	    def game_over(self):
   753	        ''' Returns `True` if the game is over and the player has lost. '''
   754	        return self.frotz_lib.game_over() > 0
   755	
   756	    def _disassemble_game(self):
   757	        ''' Prints the subroutines and strings used by the game. '''
   758	        self.frotz_lib.disassemble(self.story_file)
   759	
   760	    def _emulator_halted(self):
   761	        ''' Returns `True` if the emulator has halted. To fix a halted game, use :meth:`jericho.FrotzEnv.reset`. '''
   762	        return self.frotz_lib.halted() > 0
   763	
   764	    def _world_changed(self):
   765	        ''' Returns True if the last action caused a change in the world.
   766	
   767	        :Example:
   768	
   769	        >>> from jericho import *
   770	        >>> env = FrotzEnv('zork1.z5')
   771	        >>> env.step('north')[0]
   772	        'North of House You are facing the north side of a white house.'
   773	        >>> env.world_changed()
   774	        True
   775	        >>> env.step('south')[0]
   776	        'The windows are all boarded.'
   777	        >>> env.world_changed()
   778	        False
   779	        '''
   780	        return self.frotz_lib.world_changed() > 0
   781	
   782	    def _get_world_diff(self):
   783	        '''
   784	        Returns the difference in the world object tree, set attributes, and\
   785	        cleared attributes for the last timestep.
   786	
   787	        :returns: A Tuple of tuples containing 1) tuple of world objects that \
   788	        have moved in the Object Tree, 2) tuple of objects whose attributes have\
   789	        changed, 3) tuple of world objects whose attributes have been cleared, and
   790	        4) tuple of special ram locations whose values have changed.
   791	        '''
   792	        objs = np.zeros(64, dtype=np.uint16)
   793	        dest = np.zeros(64, dtype=np.uint16)
   794	        self.frotz_lib.get_cleaned_world_diff(as_ctypes(objs), as_ctypes(dest))
   795	        # First 16 spots allocated for objects that have moved
   796	        moved_objs = []
   797	        for i in range(16):
   798	            if objs[i] == 0 or dest[i] == 0:
   799	                break
   800	            moved_objs.append((objs[i], dest[i]))
   801	        # Second 16 spots allocated for objects that have had attrs set
   802	        set_attrs = []
   803	        for i in range(16, 32):
   804	            if objs[i] == 0 or dest[i] == 0:
   805	                break
   806	            set_attrs.append((objs[i], dest[i]))
   807	        # Third 16 spots allocated for objects that have had attrs cleared
   808	        cleared_attrs = []
   809	        for i in range(32, 48):
   810	            if objs[i] == 0 or dest[i] == 0:
   811	                break
   812	            cleared_attrs.append((objs[i], dest[i]))
   813	        # Fourth 16 spots allocated to ram locations & values that have changed
   814	        ram_diffs = []
   815	        for i in range(48, 64):
   816	            if objs[i] == 0:
   817	                break
   818	            ram_diffs.append((objs[i], dest[i]))
   819	        return (tuple(moved_objs), tuple(set_attrs), tuple(cleared_attrs), tuple(ram_diffs))
   820	
   821	    def _score_object_names(self, interactive_objs):
   822	        """ Attempts to choose a sensible name for an object, typically a noun. """
   823	        def score_fn(obj):
   824	            score = -.01 * len(obj[0])
   825	            if obj[1] == 'NOUN':
   826	                score += 1
   827	            if obj[1] == 'PROPN':
   828	                score += .5
   829	            if obj[1] == 'ADJ':
   830	                score += 0
   831	            if obj[2] == 'OBJTREE':
   832	                score += .1
   833	            return score
   834	        best_names = []
   835	        for desc, objs in interactive_objs.items():
   836	            sorted_objs = sorted(objs, key=score_fn, reverse=True)
   837	            best_names.append(sorted_objs[0][0])
   838	        return best_names
   839	
   840	    def _identify_interactive_objects(self, observation='', use_object_tree=False):
   841	        """
   842	        Identifies objects in the current location and inventory that are likely
   843	        to be interactive.
   844	
   845	        :param observation: (optional) narrative response to the last action, used to extract candidate objects.
   846	        :type observation: string
   847	        :param use_object_tree: Query the :doc:`object_tree` for names of surrounding objects.
   848	        :type use_object_tree: boolean
   849	        :returns: A list-of-lists containing the name(s) for each interactive object.
   850	
   851	        :Example:
   852	
   853	        >>> from jericho import *
   854	        >>> env = FrotzEnv('zork1.z5')
   855	        >>> obs, info = env.reset()
   856	        'You are standing in an open field west of a white house with a boarded front door. There is a small mailbox here.'
   857	        >>> env.identify_interactive_objects(obs)
   858	        [['mailbox', 'small'], ['boarded', 'front', 'door'], ['white', 'house']]
   859	
   860	        .. note:: Many objects may be referred to in a variety of ways, such as\
   861	        Zork1's brass latern which may be referred to either as *brass* or *lantern*.\
   862	        This method groups all such aliases together into a list for each object.
   863	        """
   864	        objs = set()
   865	        state = self.get_state()
   866	
   867	        if observation:
   868	            # Extract objects from observation
   869	            obs_objs = utl.extract_objs(observation)
   870	            obs_objs = [o + ('OBS',) for o in obs_objs]
   871	            objs = objs.union(obs_objs)
   872	
   873	        # Extract objects from location description
   874	        self.set_state(state)
   875	        look = utl.clean(self.step('look')[0])
   876	        look_objs = utl.extract_objs(look)
   877	        look_objs = [o + ('LOC',) for o in look_objs]
   878	        objs = objs.union(look_objs)
   879	
   880	        # Extract objects from inventory description
   881	        self.set_state(state)
   882	        inv = utl.clean(self.step('inventory')[0])
   883	        inv_objs = utl.extract_objs(inv)
   884	        inv_objs = [o + ('INV',) for o in inv_objs]
   885	        objs = objs.union(inv_objs)
   886	        self.set_state(state)
   887	
   888	        # Optionally extract objs from the global object tree
   889	        if use_object_tree:
   890	            player_loc = self.get_player_location()
   891	            if player_loc is not None:
   892	                surrounding = utl.get_subtree(player_loc.child, self.get_world_objects())
   893	                player_obj = self.get_player_object()
   894	                if player_obj in surrounding:
   895	                    surrounding.remove(player_obj)
   896	                world_objs = []
   897	                for o in surrounding:
   898	                    name = o.name.split()
   899	                    world_objs.append((o.name, 'PROPN', 'OBJTREE'))
   900	                    if len(name) > 1:
   901	                        # In the case of multi-word names, we assume first words are adjectives.
   902	                        for w in name[:-1]:
   903	                            world_objs.append((w, 'ADJ', 'OBJTREE'))
   904	                        world_objs.append((name[-1], 'NOUN', 'OBJTREE'))
   905	                objs = objs.union(world_objs)
   906	
   907	        # Filter out the objects that aren't in the dictionary
   908	        dict_words = [w.word for w in self.get_dictionary()]
   909	        max_word_length = max([len(w) for w in dict_words])
   910	        to_remove = set()
   911	        for obj in objs:
   912	            if len(obj[0].split()) > 1:
   913	                continue
   914	            if obj[0][:max_word_length] not in dict_words:
   915	                to_remove.add(obj)
   916	        objs.difference_update(to_remove)
   917	
   918	        desc2obj = {}
   919	        # Filter out objs that aren't examinable
   920	        name2desc = {}
   921	        for obj in objs:
   922	            if obj[0] in name2desc:
   923	                ex = name2desc[obj[0]]
   924	            else:
   925	                self.set_state(state)
   926	                ex = utl.clean(self.step('examine ' + obj[0])[0])
   927	                name2desc[obj[0]] = ex
   928	            if utl.recognized(ex):
   929	                if ex in desc2obj:
   930	                    desc2obj[ex].append(obj)
   931	                else:
   932	                    desc2obj[ex] = [obj]
   933	        # Add 'all' as a wildcard object
   934	        desc2obj['all'] = [('all', 'NOUN', 'LOC')]
   935	        self.set_state(state)
   936	        return desc2obj
   937	
   938	    def _filter_candidate_actions(self, candidate_actions, use_ctypes=False, use_parallel=False):
   939	        """
   940	        Given a list of candidate actions, returns a dictionary mapping world_diff
   941	        to the list of candidate actions that cause this diff. Only actions that
   942	        cause a valid world diff are returned.
   943	
   944	        :param candidate_actions: Candidate actions to test for validity.
   945	        :type candidate_actions: list
   946	        :param use_ctypes: Uses the optimized ctypes implementation of valid action filtering.
   947	        :type use_ctypes: boolean
   948	        :param use_parallel: Uses the parallized implementation of valid action filtering.
   949	        :type use_parallel: boolean
   950	        :returns: Dictionary of world_diff to list of actions.
   951	
   952	        """
   953	        if self.game_over() or self.victory() or self._emulator_halted():
   954	            return {}
   955	
   956	        candidate_actions = [act.action if isinstance(act, defines.TemplateAction) else act for act in candidate_actions]
   957	
   958	        state = self.get_state()
   959	        diff2acts = defaultdict(list)
   960	
   961	        if use_parallel:
   962	            state = self.get_state()
   963	            if not hasattr(self, 'pool'):
   964	                self.pool = mp.Pool(initializer=init_worker, initargs=(self.story_file.decode(), self._seed))
   965	
   966	            args = [(state, actions, use_ctypes) for actions in chunk(candidate_actions, n=self.pool._processes)]
   967	            list_diff2acts = self.pool.map(worker, args)
   968	            for d in list_diff2acts:
   969	                for k, v in d.items():
   970	                    diff2acts[k].extend(v)
   971	
   972	        elif use_ctypes:
   973	            candidate_str = (";".join(candidate_actions)).encode('utf-8')
   974	            valid_str = (' '*(len(candidate_str)+1)).encode('utf-8')
   975	
   976	            DIFF_SIZE = 128
   977	            diff_array = np.zeros(len(candidate_actions) * DIFF_SIZE, dtype=np.uint16)
   978	            valid_cnt = self.frotz_lib.filter_candidate_actions(
   979	                candidate_str,
   980	                valid_str,
   981	                as_ctypes(diff_array)
   982	            )
   983	            if self._emulator_halted():
   984	                self.reset()
   985	
   986	            valid_acts = valid_str.decode('cp1252').strip().split(';')[:-1]
   987	            for i in range(valid_cnt):
   988	                diff = tuple(diff_array[i*DIFF_SIZE:(i+1)*DIFF_SIZE])
   989	                diff2acts[diff].append(valid_acts[i])
   990	
   991	        else:
   992	            orig_score = self.get_score()
   993	            for act in candidate_actions:
   994	                self.set_state(state)
   995	                obs, rew, done, info = self.step(act)
   996	
   997	                if self._emulator_halted():
   998	                    self.reset()
   999	                    continue
  1000	
  1001	                if info['score'] != orig_score or done or self._world_changed():
  1002	                    # Heuristic to ignore actions with side-effect of taking items
  1003	                    if '(Taken)' in obs:
  1004	                        continue
  1005	
  1006	                    diff = self._get_world_diff()
  1007	                    diff2acts[diff].append(act)
  1008	
  1009	        self.set_state(state)
  1010	        return diff2acts
  1011	
  1012	    def _get_ram(self):
  1013	        """
  1014	        Returns a numpy array containing the contents of the Z-Machine's RAM.
  1015	
  1016	        """
  1017	        ram_size = self.frotz_lib.getRAMSize()
  1018	        ram = np.zeros(ram_size, dtype=np.uint8)
  1019	        self.frotz_lib.getRAM(as_ctypes(ram))
  1020	        return ram
  1021	
  1022	    def _get_special_ram(self):
  1023	        """
  1024	        Returns a numpy array containing the contents of the special ram addresses for the game.
  1025	
  1026	        """
  1027	        ram_size = self.frotz_lib.get_special_ram_size()
  1028	        ram = np.zeros(ram_size, dtype=np.uint8)
  1029	        self.frotz_lib.get_special_ram(as_ctypes(ram))
  1030	        return ram
